what_they_do: Ferry is an operations platform for discrete and process manufacturers (food & beverage, CPG, agriculture/feed, packaging, building materials, industrial products) that unifies plant-floor data (PLCs, sensors, historians via OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, Modbus TCP) with a workflow engine and an AI agent builder, then uses that data to automate production scheduling, troubleshooting, supply chain forecasting, and real-time process guidance. It replaces manual, paper-based production tracking and the human effort of manually reconciling OT (plant floor) and IT (ERP/business) data to make scheduling and troubleshooting decisions.
vertical: manufacturing operations software / MES + agentic AI
theme_fit_rationale: Ferry's stated architecture (Data Foundation unifying OT+IT data silos, a Workflow Engine, and an AI Agent Builder) is a textbook cross-functional, multi-system agent: it reads/writes across previously siloed plant systems (historians, PLCs, ERP) and automates decisions spanning several manufacturing functions (scheduling, troubleshooting, supply chain, quality/yield), which is Theme 2's core pattern even though Theme 2's listed use cases skew back-office rather than shop-floor. Theme 5 is a plausible secondary because Ferry's own published case study frames its wedge as digitizing unstructured, paper-based production records (pen-and-paper logs with transcription errors) and using that as the entry point to automate downstream scheduling/troubleshooting workflows, matching Theme 5's 'unstructured data as a wedge' thesis. Theme 1 (VLM-driven) was considered given manufacturing is a listed use case there, but nothing in Ferry's public materials indicates a vision/image/video component, so it was not selected.
workflow_artifacts: batch assignment and production tracking records
paper-based production tracking sheets (pre-digitization, per Ferry's own case study)
PLC / historian data via OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, Modbus TCP connectors
